newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UN says indicted Karadzic votes in Bosnia election.
newsitem.headline: UN says indicted Karadzic votes in Bosnia election.

text.p: Former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic, wanted by a UN tribunal on genocide charges, voted on Saturday in Bosnia's countrywide elections in the Serb stronghold of Pale, a United Nations spokesman said.

"The U.N. has preliminary information that (former Bosnian Serb leader) Karadzic, an indicted war criminal, voted in Pale in person today," Alex Ivanko, spokesman for the International Police Task Force in Bosnia, told Reuters.
Ivanko said he had no more details but expected an official statement to be released later on Saturday.

"My understanding is that he did vote in person," Ivanko said shortly after the 7 p.m. (1700 gmt) close of polling, except at some stations kept open to clear a backlog of voters caused by technical problems.
Karadzic, who was barred from standing in the historic postwar elections, was entitled to vote as a registered citizen of Bosnia who not been convicted of any crime.

The ultra-nationalist Serb wartime leader has been indicted by the International War Crimes Tribunal in The Hague for genocide and crimes against humanity in connection with the siege of Sarajevo and the massacre of Moslems at Srebrenica.
